purpose: Investigate the remaining elapsed-cost differences after equal construction arithmetic/allocation accounting and zero direct cache activity in the two expensive construction windows.
source_review_required: Review the installed Linux perf-event API and available per-thread user-space cycle/instruction counters. Establish safe RAII descriptor ownership, group read format, enabled/running coverage and failure reporting before creating a diagnostic driver.
proposed_scope: Use the existing unchanged main, full-cache and cache-free release libraries. Replace only the standalone quadratic probe observation wrapper to report per-phase user cycles, retired instructions, thread CPU and wall durations. Keep every fixture, mathematical expected value, witness, family order and 4096-input count unchanged. Include separately recorded empty-window controls for instrumentation cost; freeze a new balanced process order before collecting anything.
limits: This would be a distinct instrumentation diagnostic. Its observations cannot replace, pool with or erase any closed cost sample.
Do not call cycles divided by CPU time a calibrated clock frequency. Reference-cycle support is absent and user hardware events and thread CPU have different accounting boundaries.
Current powersave/governor state is not evidence of the environment during the prior runs. Do not tune hardware or host policy as part of this diagnostic.
Require full counter scheduling coverage or mark a sample unusable without deleting it; no adaptive extra runs to replace adverse or unavailable samples.
Keep exact witnesses and all original costs/native limits intact. No runtime change or admission follows from this coverage result alone.
